scope: Read-only audit of the Architect-generated JSON case generator and its preparation record against CODE-CONFIG-KERNEL-R1/R2. The absent configuration-parser candidate was not imported or executed. No candidate source, test, fixture, Git, network, connector, Vault, or prior evidence was mutated.
verdict: The generator is an independent typed-source oracle for its 64 JSON cases. It constructs declarative typed trees before emitting source, records spans from source positions rather than parser output, orders object children by UTF-8 bytes, preserves original key token spans, derives budgets from the generated node model, and delegates source metadata/snippet hashing to the existing pure helper interface. An independent generator-only replay against stdlib json.loads(parse_float=Decimal), independent metadata/snippet formulas, pointer/key ordering, spans, declarations and budgets reproduced 64/64 cases, 824 nodes, 824 value spans and 489 declarations. The preparation record's stated root self-check against stdlib and legacy helpers is consistent with this replay. No self-fulfilling or wrong expectation was found; the generator remains supplementary evidence and does not replace the separately accepted static fixture or parser acceptance suite.

checks: stdlib json.loads with parse_float=Decimal full-tree path/kind/value agreement
strict integer versus Decimal and canonical numeric string agreement
UTF-8 byte offsets and original codepoint offsets
CRLF boundary non-splitting and one-based line/column coordinates
raw span SHA-256 and normalized physical-line snippet SHA-256
JSON pointer ~0/~1 escaping and UTF-8 key ordering
children immediate-order agreement for maps and arrays
json_key declaration token/path attribution and declaration ordering/uniqueness
node, scalar, depth, declaration, array-item and object-key budget recomputation
independent_generator_only_replay.result: 64/64 cases passed without importing or executing a configuration parser.

checks.evidence: make_case builds typed scalar/array/object trees from a seeded local model, emits JSON source, and derives expected nodes from marks/declarations created during emission; no parser result is fed into expected output.

Generated inputs use valid JSON dumps for strings/keys, strict JSON numeric spellings, escaped controls, Unicode and CRLF/LF layout. Independent stdlib parsing reproduced every generated tree, key set, array order and typed value.

Object children are sorted by decoded-key UTF-8 bytes and arrays by index; declarations attach to member nodes, while root and array elements receive none. The replay reproduced all 824 paths and children lists.

Source positions count Unicode codepoints before UTF-8 encoding; byte bounds are computed from exact UTF-8 prefixes; generated nodes include original token/delimiter spans and do not split CRLF. Replay checked all 824 value spans and line/snippet boundaries.

The generator receives code_text_metadata and code_snippet_sha256 as explicit helper callables rather than reimplementing their API. The preparation record reports independent legacy-helper parity; this audit reproduced the same documented formulas without importing the dependency-bearing legacy module.

Expected budgets are computed from the generated marks. An independent recursive traversal reproduced node count, scalar count, maximum depth, maximum array length, maximum object-key count and declaration count for all 64 cases.

Seeded random.Random is local to each case; expected output is JSON-compatible. The future candidate run mutates a returned node child list, reruns the parser and checks expected output/limits, preserving the generator as an external expected source.

The generated JSON covers valid JSON values and exact source metadata/node shapes without changing R1/R2 API, limits, dynamic rules, TOML rules or accepted static-fixture authority. It is supplementary and does not claim complete acceptance coverage.

residual_boundaries: The generator is JSON-only and does not exercise TOML semantics; the accepted static fixture, R2 TOML matrix and dynamic vectors remain separate authorities.
The generator's expected spans originate from its own source emitter; the independent stdlib/span replay and recorded legacy-helper parity are required safeguards and passed.
No parser candidate exists in this review; implementation behavior, cross-check corruption, limits, refusal precedence and runtime purity remain future candidate gates.
